title: The Rich Fool
text:
A man in the crowd called out to Jesus and asked him to tell his brother to share the family inheritance with him. Jesus refused to act as a judge between them. Instead he warned the crowd to guard against every kind of greed, because a person's life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions. Then he told a story.

There was a rich man whose land produced an exceptional harvest. He thought to himself: what shall I do? I have no place to store all my crops. Then he decided. He would tear down his barns and build bigger ones, and store all his grain and goods there. Then he would say to himself: you have plenty laid up for many years. Take life easy. Eat, drink and be merry.

But God said to him: you fool. This very night your life will be demanded from you. Then who will get what you have prepared for yourself?

Jesus concluded that this is how it will be for anyone who stores up things for himself but is not rich toward God.
lesson: Planning for the future is wise, but no plan controls how much time you have. Make sure what you are building is worth having even if tonight is your last night.
people: Jesus, a man from the crowd, a rich man
location: Galilee and Judea (modern Israel and Palestinian territories)
